input: Enroll in a professional bookkeeping short course online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Bookkeeping courses range from absolute beginner to advanced topics like payroll, tax prep, or specific software — knowing the level and focus narrows the right course.
Whether this is for personal knowledge, a career change, or an employer requirement changes how formal or credentialed the course needs to be.
The user's current bookkeeping knowledge determines whether they need an introductory or intermediate course.
Budget is a major filter — free courses (Coursera audit, YouTube) vs. paid certifications (AAT, QuickBooks, NACPB) are very different paths.
How quickly they need to complete it affects which course length and pacing model (self-paced vs. scheduled cohort) is suitable.
Some learners need a recognized certificate or accreditation for employment; others just want the skills — this shapes which platforms and courses to target.
Preferred software focus (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero, Excel) can determine which course is most practically useful for the user's real-world context.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in an online professional bookkeeping course
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and enroll in a short online course that builds professional bookkeeping skills.

questions.title: What bookkeeping topics do you most need to cover?
questions.description: Identify whether the user needs general bookkeeping fundamentals, payroll, tax basics, financial statements, or a specific area — to match scope of the course.

questions.title: Is this for a job, career change, or personal use?
questions.description: Understand the purpose behind enrollment — employer-mandated upskilling, a career pivot into bookkeeping, freelance work, or managing personal/business finances.

questions.title: How much bookkeeping experience do you already have?
questions.description: Determine the user's current knowledge level — complete beginner, some familiarity, or experienced but needing formal recognition — to target the right course level.

questions.title: What is your budget for this course?
questions.description: Establish a price range to filter between free auditable courses, low-cost platforms like Udemy, or premium certified programs from bodies like NACPB or AAT.

questions.title: When do you need to complete the course by?
questions.description: Find out the user's deadline or urgency to recommend self-paced options for flexibility or structured cohort programs for accountability.

questions.title: Do you need an accredited certificate upon completion?
questions.description: Clarify whether a formally recognized credential is required — for job applications or professional profiles — versus simply acquiring the practical skill.

questions.title: Which accounting software should the course focus on?
questions.description: Identify if the user needs training in a specific tool — such as QuickBooks, Xero, Sage, or Excel — to ensure the course is immediately applicable to their work.
